title: Guidance and support for keeping backups in Google Drive
description: Product Owner request: how does a warden get a backup into Google Drive, and restore from it. THE GOOD NEWS - it already works, and needs no Drive integration. Export uses ActivityResultContracts.CreateDocument, which opens Android's own document picker; Google Drive appears there as a location like any other provider, so a warden can already save the zip straight into Drive. Import uses the matching OpenDocument picker and can read it back the same way. Nothing in the app is Drive-aware and nothing needs to be - no Drive API, no OAuth, no INTERNET permission, which matters because DESIGN.md's whole position is that the app requests no network access at all. Adding a Drive SDK would break that and is explicitly not what this ticket asks for. SO THE ACTUAL GAP IS THAT NOBODY KNOWS. The Backup screen says nothing about where the file can go, the user manual does not mention Drive, and a warden worried about losing their phone has no reason to think 'save to Drive' is available. This is documentation and a nudge, not a feature. WORTH CHECKING DURING BUILD, since it is the one thing that could genuinely be broken: whether the Drive provider reliably returns a writable stream for CreateDocument on the devices in question. Some cloud providers behave differently from local storage for new files, and a backup that silently produces a zero-byte file in Drive would be far worse than no Drive support at all. Test the round trip - export to Drive, then import that exact file back - rather than assuming symmetry. RELATED: LODGY-68's automatic daily backup needs a persisted folder via OpenDocumentTree. Whether Drive grants a durable tree permission is a real question and should be settled there; if it does, automatic backups land in Drive for free, which is the strongest possible answer to the lost-phone fear.
acceptanceCriteria: The round trip is verified on a real device: export a backup, choose Google Drive in the picker, then import that same file back and confirm the data restores intact
The exported file in Drive is confirmed non-empty and openable - not a zero-byte or truncated artefact
The Backup screen tells the warden that the file can be saved to Drive or any other location the phone offers, so the option is discoverable rather than folklore
USER-MANUAL.md documents the Drive route for both export and import, in plain language
No Drive SDK, no OAuth and no INTERNET permission is added - the app stays network-free and keeps using the system picker
Findings feed LODGY-68: record whether Drive grants a durable OpenDocumentTree permission suitable for unattended daily backups

history.note: Filed at the PO's request. Verified in code that Drive already works through the system document picker, so this is documentation plus a round-trip check, not a Drive integration.

DECIDED: build what can be built without a Google account on this machine - the Backup screen nudge telling the warden the file can go to Drive or anywhere else the phone offers, and the USER-MANUAL.md documentation for both directions. The PO will verify the round trip on a real device. The two verification criteria (export to Drive, import it back, and confirm the file is non-empty) stay open and must be signed off by the PO before this moves to Done - the whole risk here is a cloud provider returning a writable-looking stream that yields a zero-byte file, and that cannot be checked from an emulator.

Building the buildable half per the PO decision: a Backup-screen nudge that the file can go to Google Drive or anywhere the phone offers, plus USER-MANUAL docs for the Drive round trip both directions. No Drive SDK/OAuth/INTERNET - it stays on the system picker (AC5). The two Drive round-trip checks (AC1/AC2) need a Google account on a real device and stay open for the PO to sign off, as they decided.

Buildable scope complete. AC3: the Backup screen now names Google Drive explicitly in both the export and import descriptions - the file can go to Drive or anywhere the phone offers, and restore reads it back the same way. AC4: USER-MANUAL section 8 documents the Drive route for both export and import in plain language, plus the tip to point the LODGY-68 daily-backup folder at a Drive-synced folder. AC5: no Drive SDK, no OAuth, no INTERNET permission - it stays on CreateDocument/OpenDocument (the system picker), app remains network-free. DESIGN.md 4.8 records all this.

STAYS OPEN FOR THE PO, exactly as they decided (cannot be checked from an emulator with no Google account): AC1 export a backup to Drive then import that same file and confirm the data restores intact; AC2 the file in Drive is non-empty and openable; AC6 whether Drive grants a durable OpenDocumentTree permission fit for the unattended daily backup (feeds LODGY-68). These need a real device + Google account and the PO sign-off. Leaving in Testing on that basis rather than Done.

QA RESULT: the buildable half passes; the three criteria the PO reserved genuinely cannot be closed here, so this STAYS IN TESTING rather than moving to Done. Moving it would claim a Drive round trip nobody has done. 

AC5 VERIFIED HARD, because it is the one that protects the app's whole position: the MERGED manifest - what actually ships, not just what the app declares - contains no android.permission.INTERNET, and the debugRuntimeClasspath has no Drive SDK, no OAuth, no play-services-auth and no google-api client. Export and import still go through CreateDocument/OpenDocument. The app cannot reach the network. ONE THING TO KNOW, not a defect and not from this ticket: the merged manifest does carry ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, pulled in by a dependency (WorkManager) rather than declared by Lodgy. It permits reading connectivity state, not traffic, so the app stays network-incapable - but DESIGN.md says the app 'requests no network access at all', and anyone reading the shipped permission list will see a network-sounding entry. Worth a sentence in DESIGN.md so it does not read as a contradiction later. 

AC3 VERIFIED ON DEVICE: the Backup screen names Google Drive in all three places - export ('In the picker you can pick Google Drive, or any other place the phone offers'), restore ('from Google Drive, Downloads, or wherever you saved it'), and the LODGY-68 daily-backup folder. AC4 VERIFIED: USER-MANUAL section 8 documents both directions in plain language, including the '⋮ / Browse' hint for finding Drive in the picker, and the tip to point the daily-backup folder at a Drive-synced folder. DESIGN.md 4.8 records the position and the open items. 

WHAT I COULD PROVE ABOUT THE ROUND TRIP, AND WHAT I COULD NOT. This emulator has Play Services but ZERO Google accounts and no Drive app, so Drive does not appear in the picker at all - I confirmed the picker's roots were only the device, Download, Images, Audio, Videos and Documents. So AC1 and AC2 are untestable here exactly as the PO said. What I did instead was run the same mechanism to local storage end to end: exported through the system picker (file written at 11,969 bytes), pulled it, confirmed the zip's CRCs all pass and it contains a valid v7 lodgy.db (integrity_check ok) holding 3 hostels, 7 tenants, 7 invoices, 6 payments and 2 expenses. Then I deliberately wrecked the live data - renamed Sunrise PG to 'WRECKED' and deleted tenant Priya, confirmed the app showed the damage - imported that backup, and the app came back with Sunrise PG, Priya, and all 3/7/7 counts. The restore also confirms before overwriting, as LODGY-57 requires. SO: the export/import machinery is sound, and if Drive fails it will be the provider, not Lodgy. That is NOT the same as passing AC1/AC2 and I am not recording it as such - the ticket's own risk is a cloud provider returning a writable-looking stream that yields a truncated file, and only a real Drive save can settle it. 

A NOTE THAT MATTERS FOR AC6 AND LODGY-68: saving one file (CreateDocument) and granting a durable folder (OpenDocumentTree) are different capabilities, and a DocumentsProvider can support one without the other. So 'Drive appeared in the picker when I exported' will NOT answer AC6 - the PO needs to try 'Choose backup folder', pick a Drive folder, then confirm a daily backup actually lands there unattended after a reboot. If Drive does not offer tree access, LODGY-68's answer to the lost-phone fear becomes 'point it at a Drive-SYNCED local folder', which is what the manual already advises - so the documentation survives either way. 

METHOD NOTE FOR WHOEVER REPEATS THIS: pull the zip with 'adb exec-out', not 'adb shell cat'. The latter mangles binary (I got 12,015 bytes and a CRC failure that looked exactly like the corruption this ticket warns about, until I re-pulled correctly and got 11,969 with clean CRCs). A tester chasing AC2 could easily report a false defect that way.

PO SIGN-OFF GIVEN. Closing on the Product Owner's authority, which is what the ticket's own decision reserved to them - the buildable half was verified in QA and AC1, AC2 and AC6 were always theirs to settle. 

RECORDED PRECISELY, so a future reader is not misled about what was demonstrated. VERIFIED IN THIS SESSION: AC3 on the device (the Backup screen names Google Drive in export, restore and the daily-backup folder); AC4 (USER-MANUAL section 8 covers both directions in plain language); AC5 against the MERGED manifest - no INTERNET permission ships and there is no Drive SDK, OAuth or play-services-auth on the runtime classpath. Also demonstrated, though it is not AC1: the export/import machinery works end to end through the system picker to local storage - a CRC-clean zip containing a valid v7 database, and a restore that recovered a deliberately wrecked hostel name and a deleted tenant. ACCEPTED ON PO AUTHORITY RATHER THAN DEMONSTRATED HERE: AC1 and AC2 against Google Drive specifically, and AC6. This emulator has no Google account and no Drive app, so Drive never appeared in the picker; the Drive-provider behaviour the ticket was written to catch - a writable-looking stream that yields a truncated file - was not exercised in this session. If the PO ran it on their own phone, adding a line here would make the record complete. 

CARRIED FORWARD TO LODGY-68 for AC6, since it does not disappear with this ticket: saving one file (CreateDocument) and granting a durable folder (OpenDocumentTree) are different capabilities and a provider can support one without the other, so Drive appearing during an export does not establish that unattended daily backups can land there. If it turns out Drive grants no tree access, the manual's existing advice - point the daily-backup folder at a Drive-SYNCED local folder - is already the right answer, so no documentation changes either way.
